item.title: Nvidia in turmoil as China denies spying claims
item.description:
Jensen Huang during a 2025 visit to China. Zhao Wenyu/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images Nvidia is investigating whether Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Huang said he had an affair. US officials believe the woman was recruited as a spy by the Chinese government. Here's what the Nvidia CEO has said over the years about China, export controls, and the AI race. Jensen Huang's yearslong push to sell chips to China is now colliding with an affair , board investigation, and crisis at Nvidia . At the center is Alice Huang, who has been an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a company that US authorities suspect of helping China access AI chips barred by export controls . Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing. US officials believe Alice Huang, who has no relation to the Nvidia CEO, was recruited to gather information for Beijing . Nvidia's board is investigating…

item.title: France blames Iran’s Revolutionary Guards for cyber-attacks on supermarket fridges
item.description:
French foreign minister vows European sanctions against Tehran over ‘unprecedented’ hacks last month Europe live – latest updates France has said Iran’s Revolutionary Guards were behind “unprecedented” cyber-attacks on supermarket fridges in the country last month, vowing European sanctions against Tehran. “I can confirm that this attack was carried out by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” the French foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, said on Monday of the hacks on 11 and 12 October. item.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange strikes a day before U.S.-brokered talks are scheduled to begin
item.description:
US, Russian, and Ukrainian officials are expected to meet this week in Abu Dhabi for talks on ending the nearly five-year war, but experts cautioned that the meetings were unlikely to yield a major breakthrough. The first direct negotiations in nine months will address “ security guarantees for Ukraine , Europe’s post-war security architecture and economic opportunities to support Ukraine’s reconstruction,” envoy Steve Witkoff said; Washington’s efforts to end the war have been primarily focused on rebuilding commercial ties , though earlier efforts surrounding a potential Alaskan LNG terminal collapsed in response to what US investors described as secret Russian control . “As long as the White House is satisfied with small gestures rather than actual concessions, Putin will not reverse course ,” an Atlantic Council expert wrote. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Trump Orders Justice Department To Investigate His Congressional Critics, Saying They Deserve 'Imprisonment'
item.description:
Democrats who plan to investigate executive-branch officials when they take over Congress in January are "EXTORTIONISTS" worthy of "imprisonment," President Donald Trump declared in a Truth Social post on Saturday. Trump said he was "ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!" As is often the case when Trump demands the prosecution of his political opponents , he was hazy on what crime he had in mind. Although he repeatedly mentioned "extortion," that crime entails the use of threats to obtain money, property, or other things of value, so the label is clearly inapt in this context. item.title: Native American women made history in tribal, state and federal elections
item.description:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women. On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT . item.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
item.description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said. The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry. item.title: U.K. 'Looking Seriously' at Including Online Marketplaces Like eBay and Depop in Teen Social Media Ban
item.description:
Online age verification champions are a bit like horror movie villains. Once Michael Myers gets inside a house, he's not going to stop with just one or seven kills. He's going to keep killing until you push him out a window, run him over with a car, and throw his body in a lake (and even then, he'll be back again someday). Likewise, once authorities learn that the public and the courts will stand for one form of age verification—say, asking porn platforms to verify user identities—they're suddenly off on a surveillance spree that won't stop until the whole internet is covered. Age verification for app stores! Age verification for social media! Age verification for… eBay? Yes, eBay. Where your shut-in uncle buys old beanie babies and you occasionally turn for used books. Where enterprising teens might make a little cash selling their parents' old jeans. British regulators apparently want…

item.title: COP31 climate summit: Can we electrify the world?
item.description:
The UN's annual climate change summit, known as COP31, opens this Monday in Turkey amid deep concern following deadly heatwaves in Europe and deadly floods in Nepal. A "super El Niño" in the Pacific is also expected to drive more extreme weather events. In response, COP31 host Turkey is set to launch a global initiative aiming to electrify a third of the world economy. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.
